counterevidenceSearch: Directed searches and findings. (1) Fixed %HRmax vs individual thresholds: in 50 trained cyclists HR at VT1 was 81.4 +/- 3.9 %HRmax and fixed %HRmax markers showed wide individual differences (S07). In 863 tests HR at VT ranged widely across individuals while RPE at VT was about 12.5 +/- 0.9 (S08). The Norwegian %HRmax guidance comes from elite athletes and is stated to strongly overestimate the threshold range for beginners and recreational athletes (S06, Discussion). The Z1/Z2 and Z4/Z5 splits are arbitrary rather than physiological (S06; S01). This keeps the zones display-only with zoneModelConfidence LOW, keeps effort primary, and puts a disclosure for newer runners. (2) HR lag in short hard bouts: heart-rate time-in-zone underestimates high-intensity work (S01 full text; S04 abstract: time-in-zone gave 1.1%/0.8% of time in zones 2/3 versus 11.1%/2.4% of sessions by session goal). HR is a useful intensity measure only where intervals are long enough to stabilize, more than 4 min (S10). No runner-specific primary study of lag was retained (negative search). This supports no HR guidance for 5K/10K-specific work and strides. (3) Cardiac drift: HR rises progressively in prolonged exercise, more in heat and with dehydration, and then reflects a higher relative intensity (S12, S13, S15; S11: about +7 bpm per 1% body-mass loss). This supports slowing-only use and does not make a high reading in a long run spurious. (4) Race-day HR: about 20 bpm higher at race pace than at the same speed outside competition (S11). This supports no HR guidance on race days. (5) Sensor agreement: a chest strap agrees closely with ECG (S17 rc 0.996; S18 99.4% correct RR detection at high intensity); optical sensors are less accurate (S17). A gap of more than a few bpm between two maxima is therefore not mainly sensor error. (6) Lab vs field and modality: one small runner study found similar HRmax in a field test and a treadmill test (S19). HR differs between cycling and running at maximal intensity (S16; S10 cites about 5% higher HRmax in running; S09 found running produced a higher %HR than cycling at the same RPE). A lab maximum from a non-running test would bias the zones low. This added a running-modality condition to the lab reference. (7) HRmax reliability: negative search; the conflict band rests on sensor agreement and on the physiology that a genuine reading cannot exceed the true maximum, not on a reliability figure.

sources.citation: Seiler S, Tonnessen E. Intervals, thresholds, and long slow distance: the role of intensity and duration in endurance training. Sportscience 2009;13:32-53 (sportsci.org/2009/ss.htm).
sources.type: NARRATIVE_REVIEW (journal-reviewed; reviewers named on the article)
sources.locator: Table 1 and footnote; paragraph after Table 1 on 5-zone/3-zone alignment; section on time-in-zone analysis
sources.findingsUsed: Table 1 'A typical five-zone scale': HR %max 55-75 / 75-85 / 85-90 / 90-95 / 95-100, lactate 0.8-1.5 / 1.5-2.5 / 2.5-4 / 4-6 / 6-10 mmol/L. Footnote: the HR scale is slightly simplified compared with the actual scale used by the Norwegian Olympic Federation, which is based primarily on decades of testing of cross-country skiers, biathletes and rowers. Zone 3 of the 5-zone system coincides well with zone 2 of the 3-zone model; the five aerobic zones are not based on clearly defined physiological markers. Heart-rate time-in-zone analysis underestimates time spent at high intensity and overestimates time at low intensity compared with athlete perception.
limitations: the printed scale is a simplified version, not the official one

Table 2 typical HR %max: zone 1 54-73, zone 2 74-83, zone 3 84-88, zone 4 89-93, zone 5 >94, derived from average self-reported zone cut-offs of 29 elite cross-country skiers (ref 43, Sylta 2014), and 'individual adjustments are required'.

sources.citation: Seiler S. What is best practice for training intensity and duration distribution in endurance athletes? Int J Sports Physiol Perform 2010;5(3):276-91.
sources.findingsUsed: Only that elite endurance athletes typically train about 80% of sessions at low intensity (about 2 mM lactate) and about 20% at high intensity. Cited by S02 for the 5-zone to 3-zone aggregation.

sources.citation: Sylta O, Tonnessen E, Seiler S. From heart-rate data to training quantification: a comparison of 3 methods of training-intensity analysis. Int J Sports Physiol Perform 2014;9(1):100-7.
sources.findingsUsed: 29 elite cross-country skiers, 570 sessions: time-in-zone gave 96.1% of time in zone 1 and 2.9%/1.1% in zones 2/3, whereas session goal gave 86.6% zone 1 and 11.1%/2.4% zone 2/3 sessions; conversion factors 0.9/1.1 for low intensity and 3.0/0.33 for high intensity.
limitations: zone cut-offs known only through S02 and S07

sources.citation: Seiler-Viken SA, Mentzoni F, Seiler S, Skarli S, Losnegard T. Contextualizing the Norwegian standardized intensity zone framework in an international sample of endurance practitioners. Sci Rep 2025;15:34367.
sources.findingsUsed: Olympiatoppen has split the 3-zone scale into five aerobic zones; LT1 and LT2 remain the anchors; zone 3 aligns with 3-zone zone 2. The added splits within the low (zones 1-2) and high (zones 4-5) domains are arbitrary, not anchored in physiological transitions. About 80% and 88% of session peak HR at LT1 and LT2 are based on highly trained and elite athletes and are likely to strongly overestimate the threshold range for beginner and recreational athletes; a beginning runner's LT2 may correspond to 75-80% HRmax. HR without individual testing is easily misinterpreted. Survey, runners: lower limits of zones 1-5 were 55.4 +/- 10.2, 69.8 +/- 6.7, 79.6 +/- 5.7, 86.6 +/- 4.1 and 92.3 +/- 3.5 %HRmax (298 respondents using a 5-zone scale across sports).
limitations: the recreational-runner statement is a discussion inference with cited support, not a measured result of this study

sources.citation: Meixner B, Filipas L, Holmberg HC, et al. Zone 2 intensity: a critical comparison of individual variability in different submaximal exercise intensity boundaries. Transl Sports Med 2025;2025:2008291.
sources.findingsUsed: 50 experienced cyclists (30 men, 20 women, age 31.2 +/- 7.8 y, VO2peak 54.1 +/- 8.1 mL/kg/min). Zone 2 of the Norwegian Olympic Federation is defined as 72-82% HRmax (citing Sylta 2014). HR at VT1 was 81.4 +/- 3.9 %HRmax and at FatMax 72.3 +/- 5.7 %HRmax. Fixed %HRmax markers showed wide individual differences and may misrepresent metabolic responses; a 5% difference is about 10 bpm.

sources.citation: Gaskill SE, Skinner JS, Quindry J. Ventilatory threshold related to VO2 reserve, heart rate reserve, and rating of perceived exertion in a large varied sample. Med Sci Sports Exerc 2023;55(10):1876-1885.
sources.findingsUsed: 863 test records from sedentary to aerobic athletes: VT averaged 55.2 +/- 11.3 %VO2R, individuals 25.5-86.0%, and HR at VT as %HRR was very similar and not statistically different; large variance at every fitness level. RPE at VT was relatively homogeneous, 12.5 +/- 0.93, regardless of fitness or activity level.
limitations: resting HR assumed 60 bpm outside HERITAGE

sources.citation: Losnegard T, Skarli S, Hansen J, et al. Is rating of perceived exertion a valuable tool for monitoring exercise intensity during steady-state conditions in elite endurance athletes? Int J Sports Physiol Perform 2021;16(11):1589-1595.
sources.findingsUsed: 160 elite athletes: RPE related strongly to %HR, %VO2 and lactate (r = .80-.82); between-subject CV of %HR fell from about 10-15% at RPE 8 to about 5% at RPE 17; running produced a systematically higher %HR (about 2%) than cycling at the same RPE.

sources.citation: Olympiatoppen (Norwegian Olympic and Paralympic Committee and Confederation of Sports). Olympiatoppen's intensity scale, version 2 (2024), English edition. olt-skala.nif.no/olt_2024_en.pdf (authors listed by S06 ref 41: Skarli S, Svendsen I, Paulsen G, Mentzoni F, Losnegard T).
sources.locator: Table 1 (page 3); interpretation (page 4); HR benefits/disadvantages (page 19); HRmax testing (pages 25-26); I-1 (page 27)
sources.findingsUsed: Table 1 %HRmax: I-1 ~55-72, I-2 ~72-82, I-3 ~82-87, I-4 ~87-92, I-5 ~92-100. The scale is guidance, not to be applied rigidly; it is to be adapted to modality, fitness level and individual differences, and athletes should develop their own I-scales. HR is a good measure in continuous work or intervals long enough to stabilize (>4 min) and less useful in short high-intensity intervals because of the delay at onset; daily HR variation about 6-12 beats; drift in long sessions, especially in heat or dehydration; a chest strap rather than the wrist; HRmax must be accurate and updated. HRmax varies by modality (about 5% higher in running than cycling, citing Millet 2009); HRmax test of 3 x 3 min ending at maximum.
limitations: institutional guidance for Norwegian elite athletes, not peer reviewed
used only to verify the published scale values and as auxiliary context; no ruling rests on it alone

globalConditions: G.1 Additive only: heartRateZones (three zones), its rules, values and bytes are unchanged. The five zones are a separate output, heartRateFiveZones.

G.2 Display-only reference: never a session target, never a gate, never converted to pace or effort, never used to size, progress, adapt or change any dose, never called thresholds (Q6, Q6.separation unchanged).
G.3 Effort is the prescription in every session; heart rate is never primary in V1.
G.4 Heart rate may only suggest slowing; a low reading never suggests speeding up.
G.5 Missing, withheld or conflicting heart rate never blocks or changes a prescription.
G.6 No age formula, no heart-rate reserve, no optical sensor, no declared maximum without qualifying provenance.
G.7 The three approved domains LOW / MODERATE / HIGH stay the sporting categories; Z1-Z2 and Z4-Z5 are display subdivisions with no separate sporting rule in V1.
G.8 Not a safety monitor: heart-rate copy must imply no health meaning; any symptom goes to the existing warning-sign route.
G.9 Synthetic data only; no real athletes; inert until an independent SSCTR record bound to the new values file exists, and only with V1X-RUN-CAPACITY and V1X-RUN-HR on.

items.question: Is a five-zone fixed-fraction scale defensible as a display-only reference for this population?
items.evidenceStatusNote: SUPPORTED_WITH_LIMITS that the five-zone %HRmax scale is an established, published convention nesting the three LT1/LT2 domains (S01, S02, S06, S07, S10). CONFLICTING_EVIDENCE for its individual physiological meaning (S06, S07, S08, V1RC-SRC08, V1RC-SRC09); that part supports display only.
conditions: Display-only under G.2-G.5; zoneModelConfidence is always LOW.
Never presented as 'Olympiatoppen zones', 'Norwegian zones' or any named scale: the app's Z2/Z3 cut is 0.80, not the scale's ~0.82, so its Z2 and Z3 differ from I-2 and I-3.
The Z1/Z2 and Z4/Z5 splits are conventions without a physiological anchor (S06); no V1 rule may treat Z1 differently from Z2 or Z4 differently from Z5.
Disclosure that individual thresholds vary widely, and that for newer runners the same percentage can be a harder effort than the zone name suggests (S06).
items.rationale: The scale is a widely used and verifiable convention, and its 5 to 3 aggregation (I1+I2, I3, I4+I5) is stated by S02, S06 and S01. Fixed fractions misplace individuals relative to thresholds: VT1 was 81.4 +/- 3.9 %HRmax in trained cyclists (S07), HR at VT spans a very wide range across fitness levels (S08), and the elite-derived percentages likely overestimate the threshold range for recreational athletes (S06). It is therefore defensible only as a coarse descriptive reference subordinate to effort, as Q6 already decided for three zones.
items.disclosure: 'Zones are fixed percentages of your maximum heart rate. They are a rough guide, not your personal thresholds. How the run feels governs.'

items.question: Is 0.72 supported for Z1/Z2?
conditions: Convention only (HR5-1.a); the split carries no sporting rule in V1.
items.rationale: The official scale puts I-1/I-2 at ~72% (S10); S07 reports Norwegian zone 2 as 72-82% (citing Sylta 2014); S02 reports elite self-reported cut-offs of 73/74%; practitioners using a 5-zone scale put the zone 2 lower limit at 69.8 +/- 6.7 % in running (S06). 0.72 matches the published convention, not an individual marker.

items.question: Is 0.92 supported for Z4/Z5?
conditions: Convention only (HR5-1.a); Z4 and Z5 share the HIGH domain and the same role.
items.rationale: Official I-4/I-5 cut ~92% (S10); practitioner zone 5 lower limit 92.3 +/- 3.5 % in running (S06); elite self-report 93/94% (S02); the simplified Sportscience scale used 95% (S01). 0.92 matches the official scale and the survey mean.

items.question: Keep the approved 0.80 and 0.87 cuts rather than the scale's ~0.82?
conditions: The bpm of the 0.80 and 0.87 boundaries must equal the three-zone output's bpm for the same observed reference (checked for 140-220 bpm: no rounding mismatch).
items.rationale: The Founder decision forbids moving domains or creating artificial ones, and Q6 approved 0.80/0.87. Both lie within the evidence spread: elite LT1 and LT2 at ~80% and ~88% of session peak HR (S06); VT1 81.4 +/- 3.9 %HRmax (S07); practitioner zone 3 lower limit 79.6 +/- 5.7 % and zone 4 lower limit 86.6 +/- 4.1 % in running (S06); official I-3/I-4 at ~87% (S10). The cost of 0.80 rather than 0.82 is a 0.08-wide Z2 and a wider Z3, disclosed under HR5-1.a.

items.question: Should Z1 have a floor (0.50/0.60) or stay open? Z5 upper end?
conditions: Z1 open below 0.72, as LOW is open today; Z5 open above 0.92, because an observed maximum may be below the true maximum.
items.rationale: Published floors disagree (~55% in S10 and S01; 54% in S02; runner survey 55.4 +/- 10.2 % in S06; 60% for running reported by S06 from another source). A floor would add a 'below zones' state with no sporting use in a display-only reference. The request's '60-72' and '92-97' are not the official values (S10: ~55-72 and ~92-100); with open ends neither number is needed.

items.question: Request's stated basis (60-72/72-82/82-87/87-92/92-97 'for example in Tonnessen 2014 and Seiler 2010')
items.value: Basis to cite in the values file: S10 Table 1 (~55-72/72-82/82-87/87-92/92-100, official, not peer reviewed), S07 (zone 2 72-82%, peer reviewed, citing Sylta 2014), S06 (5 to 3 alignment, arbitrary sub-splits), S02 (5 to 3 aggregation; elite cut-offs 54-73/74-83/84-88/89-93/>94).
conditions: The values file and any documentation must not attribute 60-72/72-82/82-87/87-92/92-97 to Tonnessen 2014 (its Table 2 says otherwise) or to Seiler 2010 (not verified).
items.rationale: Verified in full text: S02 Table 2 reports different numbers; the Seiler 2010 table could not be accessed.

items.question: Is adding LAB_MEASURED_MAXIMUM supported?
conditions: Added: the lab test must be declared a running test (treadmill or field running). Data/Engineering choose the existing field that carries this without changing frozen bytes or shared contracts. If none exists, the lab tier stays off (LAB_MODALITY_NOT_RUNNING_OR_UNKNOWN) and five zones come only from the observed maximum.
Added: sensor CHEST_STRAP or ECG; optical, other or missing does not qualify.
Added: RPE 8 or higher reported for the test (the same maximality proxy as Q6(b)); completed not false; tolerated not false.
Kept: LAB_TEST in force under the existing lab rules (182 days, no declared break of 14 days or more since, not before a hold or return; SSCTR-V1RC-R-09), heartRate.maxBpm 140-220.
The lab's own supplied values (thresholds, etc.) stay shown as supplied in heartRateZones and are never mapped into zones or combined with them.
items.rationale: A maximal test is the usual way to obtain HRmax, and S10 recommends a measured, updated HRmax over age estimates (consistent with V1RC-SRC10, SRC11). But the app cannot verify protocol, modality or maximality (Q6.a). HRmax differs between running and cycling (S16; about 5% in S10; S09 shows running gives a higher %HR at the same RPE), so a cycle-ergometer maximum would bias every running zone low. One small runner study found similar HRmax in field and treadmill running tests (S19), so a running lab test adds a second route to the same quantity, not a superior one.
items.disclosure: 'The maximum your lab test reported, as you supplied it; not checked by the app.'

items.question: Order: lab, then observed, then none.
conditions: The order applies only subject to the HR5-3 conflict rule; with no qualifying reference, there are no five zones and a typed reason is given.
items.rationale: Lab first is acceptable because the HR5-3 rule withholds zones whenever an observed chest-strap reading contradicts the lab value. The lab value is therefore used only when it is at least as high as, or within 5 bpm of, every qualifying observation.

items.question: OBSERVED_MAXIMUM exactly as approved Q6(b).
conditions: Identical to the approved rule and value; no change.
items.rationale: Consistency with Q6(b); the chest-strap evidence was re-checked (S17, S18).

items.question: Refuse a declared maximum without qualifying effort or sensor, age formula, HRR, session average HR, optical sensors?
items.rationale: A declared maximum with no effort or sensor provenance may be an age estimate or an optical reading, both of which are poorly individual or less accurate (V1RC-SRC10, SRC11; S17). A session average is not a maximum. V1 has no resting HR for HRR.
items.disclosure: 'Zones need a maximum recorded by a chest strap in a hard effort or in a running lab test; a typed-in number is not enough.'

items.question: Lower-wins under a >5 bpm conflict?
conditions: Changed: no lower-wins. When both are in force and the highest qualifying observed maximum exceeds the lab maximum by more than 5 bpm, there are no five zones: UNAVAILABLE / REFERENCE_CONFLICT, reporting both values, dates and evidence ids.
Changed: a lab maximum above the observed maximum is not a conflict; the lab maximum is used.
Kept: within 5 bpm the hierarchy decides (lab), with no conflict.
The 5 bpm band is a DECIDED design tolerance, not an HRmax reliability estimate (negative search); it changes no session either way.
items.rationale: An artifact-free chest-strap reading cannot exceed the true maximum, and chest straps agree closely with ECG (S17, S18). An observed value well above the lab value therefore shows that the lab value is not this athlete's running maximum (for example a submaximal or non-running test, S16, S10). Lower-wins would knowingly build zones on a value below a recorded heart rate. The reverse case is expected: a 10-minute effort at RPE 8 need not reach the maximum, so an observed value below the lab value is not a contradiction. Withholding is the abstention-preferring choice, because nothing is lost for prescription (G.5). 5 bpm is well above chest-strap measurement error, so a larger gap is not explained by the sensor. Within the band the choice of reference moves the boundaries by at most about 5 bpm.
items.disclosure: 'Your lab maximum (<bpm>, <date>) is lower than a heart rate your chest strap recorded (<bpm>, <date>), so we are not showing zones. Effort governs.'

items.question: Rounding, interval convention, open ends, degeneracy check.
items.evidenceStatusNote: Arithmetic convention; no scientific claim beyond HR5-1.
conditions: boundaryBpm = floor((referenceBpm x perMille + 500) / 1000), integers only.

For an observed reference, the 0.80 and 0.87 boundaries must equal the three-zone bpm (Math.round(bpm x fraction)). This instance checked every integer 140-220 and found no mismatch and no degenerate set; the implementation must test this.
[from, to): a reading equal to a boundary belongs to the higher zone.
items.rationale: Deterministic integer arithmetic avoids floating-point edge cases and agrees with the three-zone output over the plausible range.

items.question: referenceConfidence MODERATE for a lab maximum?
conditions: Changed: referenceConfidence LOW for a lab maximum as well as for an observed one; under a conflict there are no zones, so no confidence is given.
Kept: zoneModelConfidence always LOW; estimated: true on every output.
Kept: every output names its reference (kind, bpm, evidence id, date, sensor, protocol as supplied, age in days).
items.rationale: The app cannot verify a supplied lab test's protocol, modality or maximality (Q6.a confidence LOW). A MODERATE label would imply a verification that did not happen.
items.disclosure: Reference shown with its kind, date and age.

items.question: Effort as the prescription in every session; HR never primary in V1.
conditions: No session is gated, sized, progressed or changed by heart rate; no dose changes.
items.rationale: RPE at VT is homogeneous across fitness levels (S08), while %HRmax at thresholds varies widely (S07, S08) and is likely miscalibrated for recreational runners (S06). RPE tracks %HR strongly in trained athletes (S09), and HR- and RPE-based distributions agree when HR zones come from measured thresholds (V1RC-SRC23), which V1 does not have.

items.question: EASY, LONG, RECOVERY_EASY, SHAKEOUT, EASY_REESTABLISHMENT (EASY mode): ceiling cue from Z4.
conditions: A sustained reading in Z4 or above may suggest slowing; never speeding up; effort governs.
The cue is not a safety signal and implies no health meaning (G.8).
Drift in long or hot runs is real added strain (S12), so the cue stays valid there. Copy may name heat and dehydration as reasons heart rate rises (S11, S13).
Known limit, disclosed: for newer runners Z4 is a late ceiling (S06); effort remains the guard.
items.rationale: Z4 is the start of the approved HIGH domain, exactly the Q6 'high-zone reading may suggest slowing' rule. A ceiling cue fails safe under HR lag, because lag makes early readings low, never high. Drift raises HR with real strain (S12, S13), so slowing is the appropriate response.
items.disclosure: 'If your heart rate stays in Z4 or higher on an easy run, consider slowing down. A low reading never means speed up.'

items.question: Should RECOVERY_EASY / SHAKEOUT cue from Z3?
items.value: Z4 kept for RECOVERY_EASY, SHAKEOUT and EASY_REESTABLISHMENT (no change from Q6)
conditions: Proposed for re-review (proposedQueueItems HQ-V1HR5-SSCTR-ZONES, reReviewNotes).
items.rationale: Recovery sessions share the EASY_CONVERSATIONAL effort cue (RPE 2-4) and differ only by a slower pace ceiling. Whether a reading of at least 0.80 HRmax marks a recovery run as too hard depends on individual VT1, which sits near or above 0.80 in many trained athletes (S07 81.4 +/- 3.9 %HRmax in cycling; running gives a higher %HR, S09) and lower in recreational ones (S06, discussion inference). The evidence does not support a separate cue zone for this population, and a Z3 cue would also differ from the three-zone cue text approved in Q6.

items.question: Show the zones EASY/LONG 'usually sit in' (Z1-Z2)?
items.rationale: That would convert an effort domain into a heart-rate zone, which Q6.separation refused. Individual %HRmax at the easy/threshold boundary varies too widely to state (S07, S08), and labelling Z3 as 'not easy' would contradict effort for some runners.

items.question: THRESHOLD, HALF_MARATHON_SPECIFIC, MARATHON_SPECIFIC: no HR guidance.
items.rationale: Fixed fractions are not individual thresholds, and Q6.separation keeps zones and effort domains apart. A Z5 ceiling on threshold work is plausible, since bouts of 5 min or more allow HR to stabilize (S10), but it was not requested and is not supported for this population; abstained (see abstentions).

items.question: FIVE_K_SPECIFIC, TEN_K_SPECIFIC, strides: no HR guidance.
items.rationale: HR time-in-zone underestimates high-intensity work (S01; S04 conversion factor 3.0 in the high range). HR is less useful in short high-intensity intervals because of its delay at onset and is a good measure only above about 4 min (S10). No runner-specific primary lag study was retained (negative search); withholding guidance needs less evidence than giving it.

items.question: RACE, RACE_TOUCH: no HR guidance.
conditions: Race-day guidance stays as approved.
items.rationale: Race HR is about 20 bpm higher at the same speed than outside competition (S11), and drift complicates HR feedback in marathons (S14).

items.question: WALK, WALK_JOG, FAMILIAR_REPEATED_BOUTS; WALK_JOG/RESTART/RETURN modes; hold; no zones: NONE with typed reason.
conditions: Modes and hold withdraw the zones (Q9); effort-only families carry no HR role.
items.rationale: Consistent with Q9 and the effort-only walk/jog design; intermittent walk/jog makes HR lag-dominated (S10).
items.disclosure: 'After a break we go by effort.' (Q9)

items.question: Unknown family: NO_HEART_RATE_GUIDANCE.
items.evidenceStatusNote: Fail-closed design rule; no scientific claim.
items.rationale: Fail closed.

items.question: Conflict between HR and RPE: effort governs.
items.rationale: A high HR at a low RPE has known causes that do add strain (heat, dehydration, drift: S11, S12, S15), so slowing is acceptable. A low HR at a high RPE is governed by effort.

items.question: Novices: same rules?
items.value: same rules; walk/jog stays effort only
conditions: The newer-runner disclosure of HR5-1.a is required.
No novice-specific HR cue (abstained).
items.rationale: Same rules are safe because effort governs and the cue only slows. A novice-specific lower ceiling is plausible (S06) but not supported numerically.

items.question: Any family where HR is primary guidance in V1?
conditions: HR may become primary only with individually measured thresholds, mapped by a separately reviewed rule (future).
items.rationale: No individually anchored zones exist in V1; fixed fractions misclassify individuals.

items.question: Time in zone: conditions for a future classifier.
conditions: V1 output: sessionDistribution UNAVAILABLE / NO_HEART_RATE_SERIES_IN_CONTRACT. The classifier is not wired to any input, and its existence enables nothing.
Time per zone is never derived from an average heart rate.
Future conditions are recorded under values.timeInZone.futureClassifierConditions; a future channel needs its own SSCTR and Data review.
items.rationale: Time-in-zone systematically underrepresents hard work (S01, S04), drifts upward in long or hot sessions (S12), and depends on sensor quality (S17). It is descriptive at most.

items.question: Week-boundary updates, Q9 withdrawal, replacement and expiry.
conditions: The reference and the conflict status are re-evaluated only at a week boundary, from evidence on record before the week starts.
Observed: the highest qualifying value within 365 days (Q6(b)); a newer higher one is used from the next week, and an older higher one stays until it ages out.
Lab: 182 days, never before a break of 14 days or more, a hold or a return (R-09). On expiry the observed maximum is used from the next week, if one qualifies.
Withdrawn by the Q9 events; evidence dated before a withdrawing event is not used again.
items.rationale: Consistent with the approved three-zone behaviour. HRmax declines only slowly with age (V1RC-SRC10, S10), so the 365-day window is acceptable.

values.boundary: V1X-RUN-HR-FIVE-ZONE (on only with V1X-RUN-CAPACITY and V1X-RUN-HR, and an independent SSCTR record bound to this file's bytes)
values.output: heartRateFiveZones (separate from heartRateZones, which is unchanged)

boundaryRule.bpm: floor((referenceBpm * perMille + 500) / 1000), integer arithmetic (round half up)
boundaryRule.interval: [from, to): a reading equal to a boundary belongs to the higher zone
boundaryRule.openEnds: Z1 has no lower bound; Z5 has no upper bound
boundaryRule.strictlyIncreasing: required; otherwise UNAVAILABLE / ZONE_BOUNDARIES_DEGENERATE (none occurs for 140-220)
boundaryRule.mustEqualThreeZoneBpm: for an observed reference, the 800 and 870 per-mille boundaries equal heartRateZones MODERATE lowBpm and highBpm

labMeasuredMaximum.inForce: existing lab rules: recencyDaysMax 182; no declared break of 14 days or more since; not dated before a hold or return (SSCTR-V1RC-R-09)
labMeasuredMaximum.runningModality: REQUIRED_DECLARED (treadmill or field running). The field is chosen by Data/Engineering among existing inputs without changing frozen bytes or shared contracts; absent or other gives LAB_MODALITY_NOT_RUNNING_OR_UNKNOWN
labMeasuredMaximum.label: The maximum your lab test reported, as you supplied it; not checked by the app

observedMaximum.use: highest qualifying value in the window
observedMaximum.label: The highest heart rate your chest strap recorded in a hard effort; your true maximum may be higher

conflict.appliesWhen: a qualifying lab maximum and a qualifying observed maximum are both in force at the week boundary
conflict.rule: if observedMaxBpm - labMaxBpm > 5: UNAVAILABLE / REFERENCE_CONFLICT; otherwise the lab maximum is used
conflict.bandBasis: DECIDED tolerance above chest-strap measurement error (S17, S18); not an HRmax reliability estimate

sessionUse.principle: Effort is the prescription in every session; heart rate is never primary in V1; it may only suggest slowing.

EASY_REESTABLISHMENT.onlyWhen: plan in EASY mode and zones in force

NO_ZONES.reason: the typed reason of heartRateFiveZones (e.g. NO_MEASURED_HEART_RATE, HEART_RATE_DATA_NOT_QUALIFYING, REFERENCE_CONFLICT, EXTENSION_NOT_ENABLED)

cueRules.cueFromBpm: lower bpm boundary of the cue zone for the reference in force

updating.evidenceCutoff: on record before the week starts (same rule as heartRateZones)
updating.observedReplacement: highest qualifying within 365 days; a newer higher value applies from the next week
updating.withdrawal: Q9: a declared break of 14 days or more, a hold, or WALK_JOG, RESTART or RETURN mode; evidence dated before such an event is not used again

futureClassifierConditions: Samples only from a qualifying sensor (CHEST_STRAP or ECG); optical samples excluded.
Classify with the reference and boundaries in force for that session's week; never retroactively with a later reference.
Gaps and dropouts are UNKNOWN time, never interpolated; report covered and unknown time with the distribution.
A minimum-coverage threshold for reporting a distribution is not set here; a future review sets it with the channel's Data semantics (no evidence-based number found).
No exclusion of the first minutes is required, but no rule may read early readings (HR lag at onset) or late readings (drift) as fitness, readiness or adherence evidence.

Time in zone never judges whether a harder session was hard enough and never drives adherence (G03), progression or adaptation; it underrepresents hard work (S01, S04) and drifts upward in long or hot sessions (S12).
Samples above 220 bpm, or flagged by the device as artifacts, are UNKNOWN; physiological plausibility limits for samples are a Data decision.
A future channel requires its own SSCTR and Data review before any output.

disclosures.zones: Zones are fixed percentages of your maximum heart rate. They are a rough guide, not your personal thresholds. How the run feels governs.
disclosures.newerRunners: For newer runners the same heart rate can mean a harder effort than the zone name suggests; go by feel.
disclosures.lab: The maximum your lab test reported, as you supplied it; not checked by the app.
disclosures.observed: Estimated from the highest heart rate your chest strap recorded in a hard effort; your true maximum may be higher.
disclosures.conflict: Your lab maximum is lower than a heart rate your chest strap recorded, so we are not showing zones. Effort governs.
disclosures.cue: If your heart rate stays in Z4 or higher on an easy run, consider slowing down. A low reading never means speed up.
disclosures.note: Wording is Product-owned; the meaning must be kept.

workedExamples.case: lab 182 (running, chest strap, RPE 9, 60 days) and observed 191

workedExamples.result: lab 195 used; no conflict (lab above observed)

workedExamples.case: lab on a cycle ergometer, or modality not declared, and observed 186

workedExamples.result: Z4 (boundary belongs to the higher zone)

aeReview.q1_planAdequate: Unchanged: no session, dose, phase or progression changes.
aeReview.q2_materialFact: Only a provenance-qualified maximum; none is inferred.
aeReview.q3_keepDefensible: KEEP the prescription in every case; heart rate is descriptive.
aeReview.q4_changeNecessary: No prescription change; the five zones are an additive display.
aeReview.q5_smallestIntervention: Display-only reference with a slowing-only cue in easy families.
aeReview.q6_smallerAlternatives: No five zones at all is the smaller alternative; the Founder decided five zones exist, so the smallest compliant form is display-only.
aeReview.q7_priorityAndProgression: Protected: effort governs, nothing gates or progresses.
aeReview.q9_uncertainty: Individual meaning of fixed fractions (LOW zoneModelConfidence); unverifiable lab protocol; recreational-runner calibration.
aeReview.q10_askHoldClinical: Medication or conditions that alter heart-rate response are outside this role (escalated). Symptoms use the existing warning-sign route.

changedFromProposal: HR5-1: basis corrected; Tonnessen 2014 reports 54-73/74-83/84-88/89-93/>94, not 60-72/72-82/82-87/87-92/92-97; the official scale is ~55-72/72-82/82-87/87-92/92-100; Seiler 2010 not verified. Fractions themselves unchanged.
HR5-2: lab maximum needs a declared running test, a CHEST_STRAP or ECG sensor, RPE 8 or higher reported, and completed and tolerated not false.
HR5-3: no lower-wins. If the observed maximum exceeds the lab maximum by more than 5 bpm, no five zones (REFERENCE_CONFLICT); a lab value above the observed one is not a conflict.
HR5-5: referenceConfidence LOW for a lab maximum (was MODERATE).

abstentions.item: Heart-rate targets or heart rate as primary guidance in any V1 family
abstentions.status: INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE without individually measured, reviewed thresholds

abstentions.item: Z3 cue for RECOVERY_EASY, SHAKEOUT or EASY_REESTABLISHMENT
A ceiling cue (for example Z5) in threshold or race-specific sessions
Mapping supplied lab thresholds into zones
abstentions.result: shown as supplied in heartRateZones only

abstentions.item: A numeric minimum coverage, sample plausibility window or warm-up exclusion for a future time-in-zone classifier
abstentions.result: conditions only; numbers left to a future review

abstentions.item: HRmax test-retest reliability as the basis of the conflict band
abstentions.result: band set as a decided tolerance above sensor error

escalations.what: Draft implementation files appeared in the worktree during this decision and were not inputs. They must be reconciled to these values (notably the lab conditions, the conflict rule and LOW reference confidence) before the independent implementation review.

How a LAB_TEST declares a running modality and its sensor (CHEST_STRAP or ECG) using existing inputs, without changing frozen bytes, the parallel contract or IntegrationContracts. If impossible, the lab tier stays off.

Athlete-facing copy for every disclosure. The five zones must not be called Olympiatoppen or Norwegian zones. Heart-rate copy must imply no health meaning. Product decides how the five-zone cue and the three-zone text are presented so that one session never shows two different cues.
Heart-rate and lab values are health-adjacent data; their handling is outside this role.

Medication or conditions that alter heart-rate response can make zones meaningless. Whether intake asks about this is ASK / ELIGIBILITY_UNASSESSED and a clinical-human matter, not decided here. Symptoms stay on the existing warning-sign route.

validation.arithmeticChecked: Node: for every integer reference 140-220, floor((b*p+500)/1000) equals Math.round(b*p/1000) for p = 720, 800, 870, 920, and the boundaries are strictly increasing

governance.consistencyWithV1RC: Q6(b), Q6.ageFormula, Q6.separation and Q9 are kept; the three-zone output is untouched; Q6.a lab rules are kept and extended only for the new output.
